newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia to hold presidential elections in May.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia to hold presidential elections in May.

text.p: Mongolia will hold its second direct presidential election next May, with all parties represented in parliament eligible to nominate a candidate, officials said on Tuesday.

A total of 1.2 million of Mongolia's 2.3 million people will be eligible to vote in the May 19 poll, an Election Committee official told a news conference, adding that the deadline for nominations was March 11.
Mongolia's first direct presidential elections were held in June 1993 when Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat, 55, took the top job.
Ochirbat was dumped by the then-ruling Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party (MPPR) and ran as an opposition Democrat, securing 57.8 percent of the vote.
He has refused an offer by the formerly communist MPPR to be its candidate this time, officials said, and it was not known if he would again run as a Democrat.
